keywords.def: money collected by government from people and firms
basic facilities such as roads, rail and broadband
laws made by government
value added tax, added to the price of goods

hook.text: If the government built a new railway to your town, which local businesses would gain, and why?
hook.a: Shops, hotels and firms needing staff or deliveries: better infrastructure cuts costs and brings customers.

islamicLink.text: Islam values public good: the state of the early caliphs used zakah for people in need (At-Tawbah 9:60 lists its recipients). Zakah is an act of worship, not a business tax, but both show wealth has duties attached.

starter.q: Name one public service paid for by government.
starter.a: e.g. the NHS, state schools, roads.

teach.heading: Infrastructure (1.6.2)
bullets: Roads, rail, ports, broadband
Cuts transport time and cost
Helps firms reach customers

teach.heading: Legislation (1.6.2)
teach.note: Laws protect people but add costs.

misconception.right: VAT and income tax change what every customer can spend, so all firms are affected

teach.heading: Hinge question
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll; share results; explain the right answer and the trap in the others.

check.q: A rise in VAT is most likely to ...
check.why: VAT is added to prices, so goods cost more and demand may fall.

practice.q: Explain one effect on a restaurant of a rise in the National Minimum Wage. (3 marks)
practice.a: Higher wage costs reduce profit unless prices rise; it may cut staff hours; but staff may be more motivated.
practice.model: Point: costs rise. Explain: the restaurant employs 12 staff on the minimum wage. Develop: wage bill rises, so profit falls or prices go up.

practice.q: Corporation tax is a tax on ...

independent.q: In the portal box, analyse how a new high-speed rail line could affect a hotel near a station (6 marks).
independent.a: More visitors and easier staff travel (demand up) but more competition from new hotels and disruption during building; a reasoned conclusion.
independent.model: The teacher writes the first chain: 'Faster travel brings more business visitors, so room bookings rise, increasing revenue ...'

independent.q: Extend: give one reason a government might cut income tax and one effect on retailers.
independent.a: To boost spending; shops sell more.

independent.q: Stretch: why might consumer law help honest businesses?
independent.a: It removes cheating rivals and builds trust, which supports fair competition.

exit.q: Infrastructure means ...
exit.a: roads, rail, ports and networks

exit.q: Back to our ponder: If the government built a new railway to your town, which local businesses would gain, and why?
exit.a: Shops, hotels and firms needing staff or deliveries: better infrastructure cuts costs and brings customers.

keywords.def: a tax on imported goods
a limit on the quantity of a good that can be imported
a group of countries that trade freely together
using barriers to protect home producers

hook.text: If the government taxed every imported phone, who would pay in the end?
hook.a: Usually the customer, through higher prices; UK makers might gain. That tax is a tariff.

starter.q: Minimum wage rises: a café's costs ...

teach.heading: Trade barriers
bullets: Tariff: a tax on imports
Quota: a limit on the amount imported

bullets: Groups of countries with free trade between them
Examples: the EU, ASEAN
Common external tariff on outsiders (customs union)

bullets: 1.6.3 is studied at home this half term
Higher rates: borrowing costs rise, spending falls
Taught as knowledge of the economy, never to take

check.q: A quota is ...
options: a limit on the quantity of imports
check.why: A tariff is the tax; a quota limits quantity.

practice.q: A 10% tariff is added to imported tyres costing £80 each. Calculate the new cost of 50 tyres. (2 marks)
Free trade inside a bloc means ...

independent.q: Case (pupil PDF): a UK date importer buys from Country A (no trade agreement with the UK, 8% tariff) or Country B (free-trade agreement, no tariff, higher price). In the portal box justify which supplier to use (6 marks).
independent.a: Calculations on the sheet: Country A £5.00 + 8% = £5.40 per kg against Country B £5.30; also quality, delivery and reliability; justified choice.
independent.model: The teacher works the first calculation: £5.00 × 1.08 = £5.40 per kg from Country A.

independent.q: Extend: give one reason a government uses tariffs.
independent.a: To protect home industries and jobs, or raise revenue.

independent.q: Stretch: who might lose from a quota on imported steel?
independent.a: UK firms that use steel (car makers, builders) pay more; customers pay more.

exit.q: A tariff is ...
exit.a: a tax on imports

exit.a: Usually the customer, through higher prices; UK makers might gain. That tax is a tariff.
